text:
maria_support: FYI customer reported a spike in 429s and tail latency on their Dedicated pool (blue-pool-7) starting ~2026-03-15 14:10 UTC. They see errors and timeouts when sending long-context requests.
jonah_sre: Can you paste the top-level error and a short timeline?
maria_support: Quick timeline: 14:08 normal, 14:10 spike to 429s, 14:12 autoscale attempted to add capacity but saw backoff, 14:18 requests still slow. Errors: `429 capacity_exceeded` and `502 upstream_timeout` intermittently.
amit_eng: Any KV cache eviction metrics? Sounds like long context workloads thrashing the KV store.
maria_support: From logs: `kvcache.eviction_rate=0.87`, `kvcache.fragmentation_ratio=0.63`, `kv_cache.mem_used=93%`. Also seeing `kv_reorg_count=0` — no compaction jobs kicked.
sylvia_reliability: Interesting — fragmentation high + high eviction rate means lots of small free spans, likely long-session tokens creating uneven allocations. Could cause CPU/IO hiccups during GC.
deploy-bot: [deploy-log] https://deploys.internal/redwood/blue-pool-7/deploys/289 - autoscale policy: conservative-burst (cooldown 5m), max_burst=2 nodes.
jonah_sre: That cooldown might be preventing quick scale during a noisy-neighbor long-context flood. If eviction pressure tops out, runtime starts dropping requests to preserve latency.
amit_eng: Can we reproduce quickly? Share a minimal repro that simulates long-context sessions.
maria_support: Repro we gave customer: 1) open 50 parallel sessions; 2) in each session send 1 prompt of 64k tokens (simulated by repeated token chunks) using streaming; 3) keep session alive with periodic keepalives. They run for ~8-12 minutes. Example curl:```
for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"gpt-long-16k","input":"<repeat 30k tokens>"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
```
jonah_sre: Nice. Any kernel logs around the time? OOM? lock contention?
maria_support: No OOM. Kernel shows high page faults on that node group and increased GC loops. Snippet:```
[14:11:32] kvcache: evicting 1200 entries, free_spans=142, slow_compaction=false
[14:11:33] runtime: kv_gc: scanning shards=64, reclaimed=0, fragmentation=0.62
[14:12:05] request: id=abcd status=429 reason=kv_cache_pressure
```
sylvia_reliability: Reclaimed=0 and slow_compaction=false implies compaction disabled or starved. Might be a scheduling priority bug. Have we recently changed compaction thresholds?
amit_eng: We toggled compaction aggressiveness low for Dedicated last month to reduce CPU during peak. That could explain it. I can flip it to medium and push a conservative compaction job.
jonah_sre: Short-term mitigation suggestions: 1) increase pool size + remove cooldown temporarily, 2) enable slab compaction job on the affected nodes, 3) restrict per-tenant long-session concurrency via per-route rate limit. Any objections?
maria_support: Customer is ok with temporary changes. They're sensitive to throttling but prefer service continuity.
amit_eng: I'll schedule a compaction run now and bump autoscale max_burst to +3 for this pool for 15m.
amit_eng: Running compaction cmd: `rwc-admin kvcache compaction --pool blue-pool-7 --mode=conservative`
deploy-bot: compaction job started (job id: cj-7812), target nodes: blue-pool-7-{2,3,4}
jonah_sre: Also adding an emergency rule to lower long-context concurrency: `route.limit.concurrency=10` for tenant X for 20m.
maria_support: Applied the rate limit rule. Customer reports reduced 429s after ~90s. :thumbsup:
amia_support: (typo) ignore
sylvia_reliability: Follow-ups: - investigate why compaction was effectively off; - consider per-node slab compaction cron to avoid big fragmentation; - review autoscale cooldown values vs longburst workloads.
amit_eng: I will open PR to revert the compaction downgrade and add an adaptive compaction policy tied to fragmentation_ratio.
amia_support: (typo again)
jonah_sre: Can we add a perf alert when `kvcache.fragmentation_ratio > 0.5` AND `eviction_rate > 0.5` for >2m, to auto-run compaction or trigger scale?
amit_eng: Yes, will add an automated playbook and alert. PR/alert TBD.
maria_support: Final note for the ticket: root cause likely noisy long-context sessions causing KV allocation fragmentation + compaction suppressed by config; autoscaler cooldown prevented fast capacity add -> temporary 429s. Mitigation applied (compaction + temporary burst + per-tenant concurrency limit). Customer monitoring now.
sylvia_reliability: :eyes: please add postmortem if this recurs.
amit_eng: :shipit: will follow up with config PR and alert within 24h.
jonah_sre: Thanks team. Closing slack thread when monitoring green.
